question: Which of the following pair regarding the parts of the Indian constitution is NOT correctly matched?
option_4: Services Under the Union and the States – Part XIV
solution_text:
The correct answer is Elections– Part XVII.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The question asks for the pair that is NOT correctly matched. In the Constitution of India, Elections are covered under Part XV (Part 15), not Part XVII.

• Part XVII of the Constitution actually deals with the Official Language (राजभाषा), spanning Articles 343 to 351.

• Therefore the pair 'Elections – Part XVII' is the wrongly matched pair, making it the required answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Elections are governed by Part XV, Articles 324 to 329, which also establishes the Election Commission of India.

• The Constitution is divided into 25 Parts (originally 22), 12 Schedules and around 470 Articles.

NOTE

• Fundamental Right – Part III (Option 1): Correctly matched; Part III (Articles 12–35) guarantees Fundamental Rights.

• Panchayat - Part IX (Option 2): Correctly matched; Part IX (Articles 243–243O) deals with Panchayats, added by the 73rd Amendment.

• Services Under the Union and the States – Part XIV (Option 4): Correctly matched; Part XIV (Articles 308–323) covers Services and Public Service Commissions.

question: Who is the author of the novel 'The Blue Umbrella'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Blue Umbrella' is a short novel written by the celebrated Indian author Ruskin Bond (रस्किन बॉन्ड), set in the hills of Garhwal, Himachal Pradesh.

• The story revolves around a young girl named Binya and her prized blue umbrella.

• It was adapted into a Hindi film of the same name in 2005, directed by Vishal Bhardwaj.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ruskin Bond received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1992), Padma Shri (1999) and Padma Bhushan (2014).

• Other famous works by him include 'The Room on the Roof', 'A Flight of Pigeons' and 'The Night Train at Deoli'.

NOTE

• Arundhati Roy (Option 2): Booker Prize-winning author of 'The God of Small Things'.

• R. K. Narayan (Option 3): Creator of the fictional town Malgudi; wrote 'Swami and Friends' and 'The Guide'.

• Khushwant Singh (Option 4): Author of 'Train to Pakistan' and 'Delhi: A Novel'.

question: As of July 2025, Vinai Kumar Saxena is the Lieutenant Governor of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinai Kumar Saxena was appointed the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi (दिल्ली के उपराज्यपाल) in May 2022 and continued to hold the post as of July 2025.

• He is the 22nd Lieutenant Governor of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi.

• Before this, he served as the Chairman of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Delhi, being a Union Territory with a legislature, is administered by a Lieutenant Governor under Article 239AA.

• As of 2025, the Chief Minister of Delhi is Rekha Gupta (BJP).

NOTE

• Ladakh (Option 1): Its Lieutenant Governor as of 2025 was Kavinder Gupta (earlier B. D. Mishra).

• Puducherry (Option 2): Administered by a Lieutenant Governor; K. Kailashnathan held the post in 2025.

• Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Option 4): Headed by a Lieutenant Governor, with D. K. Joshi serving in this period.

question: Which of the following organisation/body is related to Swavalambini Programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swavalambini programme is an entrepreneurship initiative launched by NITI Aayog (नीति आयोग) in collaboration with AICTE to promote entrepreneurship among students, especially women.

• It aims to instil entrepreneurial mindset and self-reliance (स्वावलंबन) among young learners in colleges and polytechnics.

• It was rolled out with support from the Ministry of Education's technical institutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

NOTE

• NHRC (Option 2): National Human Rights Commission, a statutory body established in 1993 to protect human rights.

• CIC (Option 3): Central Information Commission, set up under the RTI Act, 2005.

• NDMA (Option 4): National Disaster Management Authority, headed by the Prime Minister, for disaster management.

question: In July 2025, which scheme was launched to boost agricultural productivity across 100 districts with district-level interventions?
option_1: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (प्रधानमंत्री धन-धान्य कृषि योजना) was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2025 to cover 100 low-productivity districts with district-level interventions.

• Announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, it aims to benefit around 1.7 crore farmers by enhancing agricultural productivity, improving irrigation and facilitating credit.

• It converges 36 existing schemes across multiple ministries with an annual outlay of about ₹24,000 crore.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme draws inspiration from the Aspirational Districts Programme model of targeted development.

• Districts are selected on parameters of low productivity, low cropping intensity and low credit disbursement.

NOTE

• PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (Option 1): Rooftop solar scheme providing free electricity to households.

• Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses (Option 3): Initiative to achieve self-sufficiency in pulses production.

• Krishi Samruddhi Yojana (Option 4): Not the scheme launched for the 100-district agricultural productivity drive.

question: In Cricket, which of the following is NOT a bowl type of Fast bowling?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chinaman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The question asks which delivery is NOT a type of fast bowling. A Chinaman (चाइनामैन) is a form of spin bowling, not fast bowling.

• A Chinaman is a left-arm unorthodox spin delivery bowled by a left-arm wrist spinner that turns from off to leg for a right-handed batsman.

• Bouncer, leg cutter and in-swinger are all deliveries used in fast/medium pace bowling.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The term 'Chinaman' is associated with West Indian bowler Ellis Achong; modern exponents include Kuldeep Yadav.

• Fast bowling variations include yorker, bouncer, swing (in/out), seam and cutters.

NOTE

• Bouncer (Option 1): A short-pitched fast delivery that rises sharply towards the batsman's head.

• Leg cutter (Option 2): A fast delivery cut off the fingers to move away from a right-hander like a leg break.

• In swinger (Option 3): A fast delivery that swings into the batsman through the air.

question: Who won the first season of Ranji trophy in 1934-35?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inaugural (first) season of the Ranji Trophy in 1934-35 was won by the Bombay (बंबई) cricket team.

• Bombay defeated Northern India in the final to lift the first-ever Ranji Trophy.

• The tournament is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship (रणजी ट्रॉफी).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Ranji Trophy is named after Kumar Shri Ranjitsinhji (Ranji), the famous cricketer and ruler of Nawanagar.

• It was instituted by the BCCI; Mumbai (Bombay) is the most successful team with over 40 titles.

NOTE

• Madras (Option 2): A participating team but not the first winner.

• Northern India (Option 3): Was the runner-up, losing to Bombay in the first final.

• Holkar (Option 4): A strong team of the 1940s-50s from Indore, but not the inaugural champion.

question: The "Mission Amrit Sarovar" initiative is anchored by the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mission Amrit Sarovar is anchored/coordinated by the Ministry of Rural Development (ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय).

• Launched on 24 April 2022 (National Panchayati Raj Day), it aims to develop and rejuvenate at least 75 water bodies (Amrit Sarovars) in each district of the country.

• The mission was part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations to conserve water for the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The mission works through convergence of schemes like MGNREGA and other water resource programmes.

• Each Amrit Sarovar is to have a minimum area of about 1 acre with water holding capacity of around 10,000 cubic metres.

NOTE

• Ministry of Cooperation (Option 1): Formed in 2021 to strengthen the cooperative movement; not linked to Amrit Sarovar.

• Ministry of Education (Option 2): Handles education policy and institutions, not water body missions.

• Ministry of Earth Sciences (Option 3): Oversees weather, ocean and climate research (IMD, Mission Mausam).

question:
Which of the following is the primary objective of Mission Mausam?
I. To enhance India's capability in weather forecasting.
II. To develop high-resolution models for improved accuracy in predicting monsoon behaviour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mission Mausam (मिशन मौसम) aims to make India 'Weather-ready and Climate-smart' by boosting both weather forecasting capability and high-resolution modelling.

• Statement I is correct: it enhances India's capability in weather forecasting.

• Statement II is correct: it develops high-resolution models for better accuracy in predicting monsoon behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mission Mausam was approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2024 with an outlay of about ₹2,000 crore over two years.

• It is spearheaded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences through IMD, IITM Pune and NCMRWF.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as Statement II is also a valid objective.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as Statement I is also a valid objective.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are true objectives of the mission.

question: The International Hockey Federation, was founded in Paris in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1924.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Hockey Federation (FIH / अंतर्राष्ट्रीय हॉकी महासंघ) was founded in Paris, France in 1924.

• It was established by Frenchman Paul Léandre Léautey and serves as the global governing body for the sport of field hockey.

• Its headquarters are currently located in Lausanne, Switzerland.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• FIH organises major tournaments such as the Hockey World Cup, Pro League and the Olympic hockey events.

• India (Hockey India) is one of the most successful nations in Olympic field hockey history.

NOTE

• 1992 (Option 1): Not the founding year of FIH.

• 1932 (Option 2): Incorrect year, unrelated to FIH's establishment.

• 1988 (Option 4): Incorrect year, not linked to the federation's founding.

question: Narayanrao Rajhauns, also known as Bal Gandharava, was a celebrated exponent of which state's musical tradition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Narayanrao Rajhauns, popularly known as Bal Gandharva, was a celebrated singer-actor of the Marathi musical theatre tradition of Maharashtra (महाराष्ट्र).

• He was renowned for portraying female roles in Marathi Sangeet Natak (musical drama) in the early 20th century.

• His melodious singing made him one of the most iconic figures of Marathi stage music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was honoured with the title 'Bal Gandharva' by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

• The Bal Gandharva Rang Mandir in Pune is a theatre named in his memory.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 1): Known for Garba and folk traditions, but not linked to Bal Gandharva.

• Haryana (Option 2): Famous for Ragini and Saang folk forms, unrelated here.

• Meghalaya (Option 4): Has tribal Khasi-Garo music, not associated with Marathi theatre.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Two Lives'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Seth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Two Lives' is a memoir written by the acclaimed Indian author Vikram Seth (विक्रम सेठ), published in 2005.

• The book narrates the true story of Seth's great-uncle Shanti Behari Seth and his German-Jewish wife Henny Caro.

• It blends biography and history spanning events across the 20th century.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vikram Seth is best known for his epic novel 'A Suitable Boy' and the novel-in-verse 'The Golden Gate'.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2007 and the Sahitya Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Chetan Bhagat (Option 2): Author of 'Five Point Someone' and 'Two States'.

• Sudha Murty (Option 3): Writer and philanthropist, author of 'Wise and Otherwise' and 'How I Taught My Grandmother to Read'.

• Samit Basu (Option 4): Indian author known for fantasy/science fiction works like 'The Simoqin Prophecies'.

question: The Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site is in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahabodhi Temple is located at Bodh Gaya in the state of Bihar (बिहार).

• It marks the spot where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment (Bodhi) under the Bodhi Tree.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The present temple structure largely dates to the Gupta period (5th–6th century CE), built of brick.

• Bodh Gaya is one of the four holiest sites in Buddhism, along with Lumbini, Sarnath and Kushinagar.

NOTE

• Haryana (Option 1): Home to sites like the Sun Temple and battlefields of Kurukshetra, not the Mahabodhi Temple.

• Punjab (Option 3): Known for the Golden Temple at Amritsar, not Mahabodhi Temple.

• Assam (Option 4): Famous for the Kamakhya Temple and Kaziranga, not associated with Bodh Gaya.

question: The Feroz Shah Kotla Fort, also known as the home of the djinns, was built in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1354.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Feroz Shah Kotla Fort in Delhi was built in 1354 by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq (फिरोज शाह तुगलक).

• It served as the citadel of Firozabad, the fifth city of Delhi established by him.

• It is popularly known as the 'home of the djinns' because people believe djinns reside there and leave letters seeking blessings.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The fort houses one of the Ashokan Pillars (from Topra), relocated here by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1351 to 1388 and was known for public works and canals.

NOTE

• 1321 (Option 1): The year the Tughlaq dynasty was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, not the fort's construction year.

• 1267 (Option 3): Incorrect year, unrelated to the fort.

• 1492 (Option 4): Associated with Columbus's voyage, not the Feroz Shah Kotla Fort.

question: Which of the following cities is NOT one of the traditional locations for the Kumbh Mela?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Varanasi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The question asks which city is NOT a traditional Kumbh Mela site. Varanasi (वाराणसी) is NOT one of the four traditional locations.

• The Kumbh Mela is traditionally held at four places: Prayagraj (Allahabad), Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.

• Varanasi, though a major Hindu pilgrimage city on the Ganga, does not host the Kumbh Mela.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Kumbh Mela rotates among the four sites on the banks of the Ganga (Haridwar), Shipra (Ujjain), Godavari (Nashik) and the Sangam (Prayagraj).

• It was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.

NOTE

• Ujjain (Option 1): Hosts the Kumbh Mela (Simhastha) on the banks of the Shipra river in Madhya Pradesh.

• Nashik (Option 2): Hosts the Kumbh Mela on the banks of the Godavari river in Maharashtra.

• Haridwar (Option 3): Hosts the Kumbh Mela on the banks of the Ganga in Uttarakhand.

question: A communication satellite acts like a television tower placed at a height of _____ km.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 36000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A geostationary communication satellite is placed at a height of about 36,000 km above the Earth's equator, so it acts like a very tall television tower (टेलीविजन टॉवर).

• At this altitude the satellite's orbital period equals the Earth's rotation period (24 hours), so it appears stationary relative to the ground.

• This allows continuous relay of TV, telephone and internet signals over a fixed region.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The geostationary orbit lies in the equatorial plane at roughly 35,786 km, commonly rounded to 36,000 km.

• The concept of geostationary communication satellites was popularised by writer Arthur C. Clarke.

NOTE

• 1000 km (Option 1): Corresponds to low Earth orbit heights, not geostationary communication satellites.

• 1500 km (Option 2): Too low for a geostationary satellite.

• 22000 km (Option 3): Closer to medium Earth orbit (e.g., navigation satellites), not the geostationary height.

question: The Aditya L-1 mission of ISRO was launched in which of the following year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ISRO's Aditya-L1 mission (आदित्य एल-1), India's first dedicated solar observatory, was launched on 2 September 2023.

• It was launched aboard the PSLV-C57 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

• The spacecraft was placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange point L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Aditya-L1 carries seven payloads to study the photosphere, chromosphere and corona of the Sun.

• It reached its halo orbit around L1 on 6 January 2024.

NOTE

• 1999 (Option 1): Incorrect; ISRO had no solar mission then.

• 2013 (Option 2): The year the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) was launched, not Aditya-L1.

• 2017 (Option 3): The year ISRO launched a record 104 satellites in one go, but not Aditya-L1.

question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pascal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The SI unit of pressure is the Pascal (पास्कल), symbol Pa.

• One pascal is defined as one newton of force acting per square metre of area (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).

• It is named after the French scientist Blaise Pascal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 101325 Pa (1 atmosphere).

• Other pressure units include bar, atmosphere and torr.

NOTE

• Ampere (Option 1): SI unit of electric current.

• Watt (Option 2): SI unit of power.

• Newton (Option 4): SI unit of force.

question: The Chandrayaan-2 mission consisted of an orbiter, a lander named _____, and a rover named _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram, Pragyan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's Chandrayaan-2 mission (launched 2019) comprised an orbiter, a lander named Vikram (विक्रम) and a rover named Pragyan (प्रज्ञान).

• The lander Vikram was named after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space programme.

• The rover Pragyan (meaning 'wisdom' in Sanskrit) was designed to move on the lunar surface and analyse the soil.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chandrayaan-2 was launched on 22 July 2019 by the GSLV Mk III rocket.

• The Vikram lander suffered a hard landing in September 2019, but the orbiter continues to function successfully.

NOTE

• Pragyan, Vikram (Option 1): Correct names but in the wrong order (rover named first, lander second).

• Bheem, Shakti (Option 3): Not the names of Chandrayaan-2's lander or rover.

• Aditya, Surya (Option 4): Solar-themed names, not associated with Chandrayaan-2.

question: Which global entity designated 2025 as the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology?
solution_text:
The correct answer is UN.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The United Nations (UN / संयुक्त राष्ट्र) General Assembly proclaimed 2025 as the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology (IYQ).

• The declaration marks 100 years since the initial development of quantum mechanics in 1925.

• It aims to raise global awareness of the importance of quantum science for development and technology.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The UN was founded in 1945 and is headquartered in New York, USA.

• UNESCO is the lead UN agency implementing the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology.

NOTE

• WTO (Option 2): World Trade Organization, which regulates international trade, not scientific years.

• OECD (Option 3): Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, an economic policy body.

• NATO (Option 4): North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance.

question: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority was established in India in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2003.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA / पेंशन निधि विनियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण) was established in India in 2003.

• It was initially set up through a government resolution to regulate and develop the pension sector.

• It was later given statutory status by the PFRDA Act, 2013.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PFRDA regulates the National Pension System (NPS) and the Atal Pension Yojana (APY).

• Its headquarters are located in New Delhi.

NOTE

• 1992 (Option 1): The year SEBI got statutory status, not PFRDA's establishment.

• 2009 (Option 3): The year the NPS was opened to all citizens, but PFRDA was set up earlier.

• 2012 (Option 4): Not the year PFRDA was established.

question: Which of the following is referred as Public sector unit (PSU) disinvestment?
option_3: Allowing direct foreign direct investment in PSU
option_4: Allowing indirect foreign direct investment in PSU
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sale of shares in PSU.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disinvestment (विनिवेश) refers to the sale (or dilution) of the government's shares/equity in a Public Sector Unit (PSU).

• Through disinvestment, the government reduces its ownership stake by selling shares to private players or the public.

• It is used to raise revenue, reduce fiscal burden and improve efficiency of public enterprises.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Disinvestment can be minority (government keeps majority stake) or strategic (management control is transferred).

• In India, the process is handled by DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) under the Ministry of Finance.

NOTE

• Purchase of share in PSU (Option 2): Opposite of disinvestment; it increases government/investor holding.

• Allowing direct foreign direct investment in PSU (Option 3): Refers to inflow of foreign capital, not the sale of government equity.

• Allowing indirect foreign direct investment in PSU (Option 4): Relates to FDI routes, not disinvestment.

question: What is the maximum number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, allowed in the Council of Ministers as per the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 of constitution of India?
option_1: 10% of the total strength of Parliament
option_2: 12% of the total strength of the House of the People
option_3: 15% of the total strength of the House of the People
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15% of the total strength of the House of the People.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 (91वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम), the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers must not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

• This provision was added through Article 75(1A) to curb the size of jumbo ministries.

• A similar 15% cap applies to state councils of ministers (with a minimum of 12 ministers) under Article 164(1A).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 91st Amendment also strengthened anti-defection provisions in the Tenth Schedule.

• A defected member is disqualified from holding a ministerial or remunerative political post.

NOTE

• 10% of the total strength of Parliament (Option 1): Incorrect figure and wrong reference base.

• 12% of the total strength of the House of the People (Option 2): 12 is the minimum for state ministries, not the Lok Sabha cap percentage.

• No constitutional limit is prescribed (Option 4): Incorrect, as the 91st Amendment introduced a definite 15% ceiling.

question: Which type of reactions are driven by the energy provided by ATP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Endothermic reactions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Endothermic reactions (आंतरोष्मी/ऊष्माशोषी प्रतिक्रियाएं) absorb energy, and in cells this energy is often supplied by ATP (adenosine triphosphate).

• ATP releases energy when it breaks down to ADP, which drives energy-requiring (endergonic/endothermic) biochemical reactions.

• Such reactions include synthesis of biomolecules, muscle contraction and active transport.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• ATP is called the 'energy currency of the cell'.

• The energy is stored in its high-energy phosphate bonds, released on hydrolysis to ADP and inorganic phosphate.

NOTE

• Neutral reactions (Option 1): Not a standard category of energy-driven biochemical reactions.

• Redox reactions (Option 2): Involve transfer of electrons (oxidation-reduction), not specifically ATP-driven energy input.

• Exothermic reactions (Option 4): Release energy rather than requiring energy input from ATP.

question: Some of the earliest works in Tamil, known as Sangam literature, were composed around _____ years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2300.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Some of the earliest works in Tamil, known as Sangam literature (संगम साहित्य), were composed around 2300 years ago.

• The Sangam age is generally dated to roughly 300 BCE to 300 CE, corresponding to about two millennia and a bit more before the present.

• This body of classical Tamil poetry was produced in poets' assemblies (Sangams) in ancient South India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sangam literature is broadly classified into Aham (love/inner life) and Puram (war/public life) themes.

• Famous works include the Ettuthogai (Eight Anthologies) and Pattupattu (Ten Idylls).

NOTE

• 6500 (Option 1): Far too early; predates the Sangam age by thousands of years.

• 5000 (Option 2): Corresponds more to the Indus Valley era, not Sangam Tamil literature.

• 3300 (Option 4): Too early for the composition of Sangam literature.
